subject: Intermittent TLS failures after on‑prem Redwood Private deploy — networking deep dive

Subject: [GlacierAI] Intermittent TLS failures after Private deploy

Rishi,

We cut over the on‑prem box to the Redwood Private appliance late yesterday and are seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures when our app calls the /v1/generate endpoints. From our side:
- Ping to the appliance VIP is fine, tcpdump shows SYN,SYN-ACK for some flows then immediate RSTs for others.
- Clients behind our corporate firewall see spiky failures at ~300–400 requests/min; retries succeed.
- Traceroute shows one hop with "ICMP frag needed" on some paths.

I've attached a packet capture and the traceroute. We also noticed that when we force smaller MSS on a test client (1400) the failures disappear. No config changes were made to Redwood since the SLA signoff.

Can you help triage? We have a maintenance window tomorrow morning if needed.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Network & Infrastructure
GlacierAI

Samir — thanks for the quick signal and attachments, this helps. High‑level: this smells like a PMTU/fragmentation issue lining up with a NAT device that drops ICMP "fragmentation needed" or a misconfigured MTU on the tunnel. We'll need:
- tcpdump on both sides showing TCP handshake + MSS/DF bits (you provided a good start).
- output of `show route table` on the on‑prem router and the firewall rules that touch ephemeral ports.
- the current NAT/translation config (SNAT/DNAT) for the appliance gateway.

I'll loop in Dev to run an overlay check and propose a short mitigation (MSS clamp or temporarily lower MTU on the Redwood interface) while we root cause. Are you available for a remote session tomorrow at 08:00 PT?

—Rishi

Quick notes from a networking/serving runtime angle — posting internal diagnostic checklist and commands that will speed root cause:
1) PMTU/DF behavior: look for DF bit set combined with ICMP type 3 code 4 from any intermediate device. If corporate FW drops those ICMPs, PMTU discovery will fail.
2) Asymmetric routing: if return traffic egresses a different NAT device without the session state, you'll see RSTs. Check route tables for the subnet that backs the Redwood VIP.
3) NAT session timeout / port remapping: our runtime keeps long connections; if there is an SNAT port exhaustion or a firewall rewriting ephemeral ports, TLS client/server tuple mismatch occurs.

Useful commands (Linux):
- sudo tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443 and host <REDACTED>' -w /tmp/issue.pcap
- ip route show table all
- sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
- show run | include route|ip nat

If you can share the pcap and a small config snippet, I can look for DF bits, MSS options during SYN/ACK, and any RST pattern. Short mitigation options: 1) MSS clamp at 1400 on the tunnel/VPN; 2) temporary SNAT translation to preserve 1:1 state (less ideal); 3) ensure intermediate firewall allows "fragmentation needed" ICMP.

I can join the 08:00 PT call.
—Dev

Thanks Rishi/Dev — attaching the fuller pcap and the traceroute output. Observations from our firewall team:
- We see ICMP type 3 code 4 from a transit hop on our provider side, but our corporate firewall silently drops that ICMP before it reaches the client during some windows (policy enforcement box).
- When we set client MTU to 1436 or clamp MSS to 1360, all handshakes succeed.
- NAT is performed at our edge GW and also at the appliance (intentional double NAT for audit reasons). That may explain asymmetric session state.

Attachments: pcap_export_20260619.pcap, traceroute-2026-06-19.txt

Can you confirm whether the Redwood appliance is setting DF on egress or whether we should apply MSS clamp on the tunnel? We want the minimal change that will restore prod traffic ASAP.

—Samir

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [GlacierAI] Intermittent TLS failures after Private deploy

Follow up post‑call and patch: we validated the root cause as PMTU discovery failing because an intermediate firewall was dropping ICMP type 3/code 4 while double NAT created asymmetric egress for some flows. Actions taken:
- Glacier applied MSS clamp of 1360 on the VPN tunnel at 05:32 PT (maintenance window).
- Redwood temporarily disabled SNAT at the appliance for the customer subnet to preserve symmetric return paths while we coordinate a permanent solution.
- Dev verified via packet captures that SYN/SYN-ACK MSS options now align and no DF‑related ICMPs are being dropped.

Next steps:
1) Glacier to work with transit provider to allow ICMP fragmentation needed (longer term).
2) Redwood SOC/engineering to review appliance NAT behavior and propose a config that avoids double NAT for customer subnets (target: design doc by 2026-06-25).
3) Post‑mortem and a brief note to Glacier execs summarizing timeline and mitigation.

I'll own the follow up and share the doc + test script. Please reply if anything missing.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
